'''Fishing junk''' is the least valuable category of [[fishing]] loot. A catch in open water is junk 10% of the time in most biomes (10.5% out of open water, where treasure can't be caught), less with {{MCW|Luck of the Sea}}, and 95% of the time in Mushroom Fields and the [[Hell]] and [[The End|End]] biomes, which have no fish.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing.json}}</ref>

Before {{Version|1.12.5}} the junk table couldn't be loaded: a trailing comma after the fish bones entry made the file invalid JSON, so in 1.12.4 a junk catch gave nothing. 1.12.5 removed the comma, and junk catches give items again.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/junk.json}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.5|quote=Fishing Junk LT Fixed (Not for modded biomes)}}</ref> Biomes added by other packs or mods are in none of the pack's fishing biome tags, so, like the Snowy Beach, they only get the base junk and treasure entries (see [[Fishing#Other biomes]]).<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing.json}}</ref>

== Loot ==

Jungles are Jungle, Sparse Jungle and Bamboo Jungle. Swamps are Swamp and Mangrove Swamp. Multiply a share by 0.1 for its chance per catch in a fish biome (for example, a lily pad is 2.18% of all catches). Fish bones come from their own loot table, <code>matcha:materials/fish_bones</code>, which builds them on an {{MCW|Ender Pearl|ender pearl}} instead of a bone, so junk fish bones can be thrown like a pearl, don't work as a bone, play no catch sound and don't unlock the [[Angler's Almanac]] entry (see [[Known bugs]]).<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/materials/fish_bones.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/fishing_sounds/fish_bones.json}}</ref>

Estus Ash was added to junk so that players on Peaceful can get it.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.1-alpha|quote=Estus Ash added to Junk pool (For peaceful players)}}</ref> Most junk plays the junk [[fishing sounds|catch sound]]. Nautilus shells, axolotls, frogs and tadpoles have their own, and junk fish bones have none.
